# Code review: relayer routing via `relayerType` from the chain config

This was a full review with no cleanup step, run under your cap of two helper agents. One agent did the testing pass and I did the other eight passes myself. Findings were not put through the two-agent validate-and-refute check, which needs two agents for each finding. I checked every finding myself against the code, but by the review's own rules there is **no score**.

**Scope:** 25 files, +487 −406 · base `ab3a736` (where `e88f197` and HEAD branch apart) → HEAD `8ed1fc2`, committed changes only · 1 commit. The repo is safe-client-gateway (TypeScript/NestJS, jest, biome) and has 3 written code rules in AGENTS.md.

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **Fix before merging.** One P1 rollout break and one P2 crash. |
| Score | Not produced, because no finding got the two-agent check. |
| Fix first | #1 (chains without a relayer type now get 403 instead of the old fallback) and #2 (a mismatched no-fee-campaign setup crashes with a 500) |

## Must fix

**#1 · P1 · Regression: chains with no `relayerType` now reject relay requests instead of falling back to the daily-limit relayer**
`src/modules/relay/domain/relay.manager.ts:59-60` (and `src/modules/chains/domain/entities/schemas/chain.schema.ts:108`, `src/modules/fees/routes/fees.service.ts:55-56`)
- **What:** the old code fell back to `DailyLimitRelayer` when no rule matched a chain. The new `default:` branch throws `NoRelayerDefinedError` (403). `.catch(null)` turns a missing, unknown or misspelled `relayerType` into `null`, so all of those cases hit that branch.
- **Failure:** this deploys before the config service sends `relayerType` for each chain that needs it. Every `POST /v1/chains/:id/relay` and `GET /v1/chains/:id/relay/:safe` on those chains then returns 403. Fee preview also returns 400 on the chains that used to be listed in `RELAY_FEE_CHAIN_IDS`. The environment variables that controlled this are removed in the same change, so there is no switch to turn the old behaviour back on.
- **Fix:** make sure the config service is populated before this deploys, and say so in the PR. Better still, keep a fallback until then (for example, `null` goes to `DailyLimitRelayer`, or an environment-controlled default). Log a warning when `.catch(null)` swallows a value it doesn't recognise, so a typo doesn't quietly stop relaying on a chain.

**#2 · P2 · Bug: a chain marked `NO_FEE_CAMPAIGN` with no campaign config crashes the relay with a 500**
`src/modules/relay/domain/relayers/no-fee-campaign.relayer.ts:81-82`, now reachable from `src/modules/relay/domain/relay.manager.ts:55`
- **What:** `relay()` reads `this.relayConfiguration[chainId].maxGasLimit` without checking that the entry exists. Before this change, the manager only picked this relayer when that entry existed. Now the choice comes from the config service, which is set up separately from the `relay.noFeeCampaign` environment config. `canRelay` (lines 43-45) and `getRelaysRemaining` (lines 131-135) in the same file already have the check.
- **Failure:** the config service sets `NO_FEE_CAMPAIGN` for a chain before its `RELAY_NO_FEE_CAMPAIGN_*` variables exist. The relay call then hits a `TypeError` that no exception filter catches, and the client gets a 500 that isn't documented.
- **Fix:** add the same missing-config check `relay()`'s siblings use and reject with a controlled error. Add a test that sets `relayerType` without the campaign config.

## Worth a ticket or a quick fix

| # | Pri | Area | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | P2 | testing | `src/modules/relay/domain/exception-filters/relayer-not-available.exception-filter.ts:13` | The new 403 path (for `null` and `GTF`) isn't tested at the HTTP level on either endpoint. `relayerTypeForChainId` in `relay.controller.integration.spec.ts:80-88` can never return `null` for the chain IDs that spec uses, and `GTF` and `RELAY_FEE` never appear in it. Only `relay.manager.spec.ts` covers the thrown errors, and only in isolation. |
| 4 | P2 | testing | `src/modules/chains/domain/entities/schemas/chain.schema.ts:108` | The `.catch(null)` fallback has no test. `chain.schema.spec.ts` never mentions `relayerType`, and removing `.catch` breaks no test. Add tests for an unknown string, each real value and `null`, following the existing `zk` tests. |
| 5 | P3 | conventions | `.env.sample.json:1191`, `.env.sample.json:1197` | The removed `RELAY_DAILY_LIMIT_CHAIN_IDS` (still marked `required: true`) and `RELAY_FEE_CHAIN_IDS` are still documented. Anyone deploying from this file will set variables that do nothing. |
| 6 | P3 | architecture | `src/modules/chains/domain/entities/schemas/chain.schema.ts:6` | The chains schema, which a lot of other code depends on, now imports from `modules/relay`, while relay imports `ChainsModule`. There's no cycle between files today, but the chain config's own value set lives in a consumer module. Moving `RelayerType` into `modules/chains/domain/entities` would fix the direction. |
| 7 | P3 | testing | `src/modules/relay/domain/relay.repository.ts:28`, `:46`; `src/modules/fees/routes/fees.service.ts:55` | Relay and fee preview now call `getChain` first, but no test covers a config-service 404 or 5xx on these paths. The repo already has a pattern for this in `recipient-analysis.service.spec.ts`. |
| 8 | P3 | kiss | `src/modules/relay/domain/exception-filters/relayer-not-available.exception-filter.ts:13-26` | Both errors already extend `ForbiddenException`, so Nest returns 403 without this filter. The filter only removes the `error` field from the body. Either drop it, or keep it and give it a test (#3). |
| 9 | P3 | conventions | `src/modules/relay/routes/relay.controller.ts:211-212` | `GET :safeAddress` can now return 403, but it has no `@ApiForbiddenResponse`, so Swagger doesn't show that response. The POST endpoint already documents its 403 (line 84). |

## Not sure about these

- **Import order:** `src/modules/fees/routes/fees.service.ts:13-15` and `src/modules/relay/routes/relay.controller.ts:45` move imports out of alphabetical order. Biome 2 sorts imports by default when `biome check` runs, so `yarn lint` would probably reorder them. I couldn't run lint to confirm.
- **Type alias:** `src/modules/relay/domain/relay.manager.ts:7` imports `RelayerType as RelayerTypeValue`, but the interface just uses `RelayerType` for both the value and the type. The alias isn't needed.

## Ruled out

- **Random `relayerType` in `chainBuilder` making tests flaky:** every chain built in the relay and fees specs pins the value, and the chains API response entity doesn't expose the field.
- **The passkey-signer bypass:** it runs before the `null` and `GTF` checks, and `relay.manager.spec.ts` covers every branch.
- **Removed `enabledChainIds` checks in `relay-fee.relayer.ts`:** the manager now does that gating.
- **Relay newly depending on the config service:** it already did, through `LimitAddressesMapper` → safe repository → transaction API.

## What this review didn't cover

- Nothing was run: no tests, lint or type-check. Every finding comes from reading the code.
- Only the testing pass had its own agent. I ran security, bugs, regression, architecture, performance, DRY, simplicity and conventions myself. Security and performance turned up nothing.
